A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States. All 34 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling experiments on the Pile and Books3, component ablations, and latency and throughput benchmarks, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original language-modeling experiments, ablations and systems benchmarks in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The TTT-Linear/TTT-MLP architectures, learned reconstruction task, mini-batch updates and inference procedures are retained. Section 2.5 corrects algebra for the existing dual form, aligning it with the unchanged primal formulation and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate language modeling on the Pile at 2k/8k context and Books3 at context lengths from 1k to 32k. No dataset or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Transformer, Mamba, the pretrained and fine-tuned Transformer variants, and the original/improved linear-attention comparisons in Table 1.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training budgets, tokenizer, context selection, FLOP matching, perplexity evaluation and systems benchmarking protocols remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix C.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 1, mini-batch-size analysis in Figure 8, backbone comparisons, layerwise losses and context-length analyses are retained without changes.

E5.justification: The training-run statement in Section 3.2 and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and plotted results are unchanged, including appendix Figures 17–20. Table 1 retains perplexities of 15.91 for original linear attention and 11.09 for the final TTT-Linear configuration.

T1.justification: Sections 2.4–2.5 correct summation/token indices and dual-form algebra. Equation 7 and delta_t now use x_s^T x_t; Delta changes from mask(X^T X)(W0 X - X) to (W0 X - X)mask(X^T X), and the mask changes from lower to upper triangular. These are localized mathematical corrections; the equivalence theorems and appendix derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain the same claims about expressive hidden states, linear complexity, comparative performance, long-context behavior and hardware efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of backbone effects, context-length trends and scaling behavior are unchanged, as are limitations concerning resources, TTT-MLP memory I/O and preliminary systems optimization.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions and training configurations in Section 2.7, Section 3.3 and Appendix C are unchanged. The embedded JAX and PyTorch code links are identical.

R1.justification: Section 4 preserves the same positioning relative to modern RNNs, test-time training, fast weights and meta-learning. All 81 references are retained unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 fixes a duplicated article, grammar and punctuation, updates the correspondence email and equation references, and adds Hyperbolic Labs and Ben Spector to acknowledgements. Section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2's caption receives a grammatical correction, with limited local text reflow elsewhere. All figures and tables retain their graphical content, structure, axes, legends and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects erroneous matrix order, mask orientation and token indices in the dual-form derivation, improving mathematical accuracy and consistency with the retained primal formulation and Appendix A. The empirical evidence, method scope and limitations are unchanged, so the overall quality gain is localized.
